tagline: Copernicus's hometown on the Vistula is a UNESCO-listed Gothic old town of brick churches, a leaning tower and gingerbread baked to centuries-old recipes.
overview: Toruń was founded by the Teutonic Knights in the 13th century and grew rich as a Hanseatic trading town on the Vistula. It was barely damaged in World War II, so its Gothic brick churches, granaries and merchants' houses survive, and the medieval town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Nicolaus Copernicus, the astronomer who put the Sun at the centre of the solar system, was born here in 1473, and his house is a museum. The Old Town Hall's tower gives views over the rooftops, and the Leaning Tower, part of the old walls, tilts noticeably.

Toruń is also Poland's gingerbread town. Piernik has been baked here since the Middle Ages, and the Living Museum of Gingerbread lets visitors make their own. Evening walks along the Vistula boulevard show the old town's skyline from the river.
